title: Savannah vs Charleston: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: If you crave a slightly more bohemian, relaxed vibe with an open-container policy and a penchant for the quirky, Savannah is your pick (budget around $150-$250/day). categories.name: h2 id="history-culture">🏛️ History & Culture
categories.summary: Both offer incredible historical experiences, just with different feels and focuses, making it impossible to pick a clear winner.

categories.name: h2 id="nightlife">🍻 Nightlife

categories.summary: Charleston's proximity to a wider variety of distinct and beautiful beaches offers superior coastal experiences.

categories.name: h2 id="costs-budget">💰 Costs & Budget

faq.question: Which city is better for a romantic getaway?
faq.answer: Both are incredibly romantic! Savannah, with its intimate squares, open-container walks, and cozy B&Bs, offers a slightly more whimsical and relaxed romance. Charleston, with its fine dining, luxurious hotels, and elegant carriage rides, leans into a more classic and refined romantic escape. It truly depends on your preferred romantic style.

faq.question: Is it easy to travel between Savannah and Charleston?
faq.answer: Yes, absolutely! The drive is a straightforward 2-hour journey on US-17 N. You can rent a car, or consider taking a bus (e.g., Greyhound) or a private shuttle service. Many travelers combine both cities into one trip, spending 3-4 days in each for a comprehensive Lowcountry experience.

faq.question: Which city has better food for vegetarians/vegans?
faq.answer: Charleston generally offers more diverse and upscale dining options, which often translates to more sophisticated and varied choices for vegetarians and vegans. While Savannah has options, Charleston's larger culinary scene makes it easier to find dedicated plant-based menus or restaurants with extensive vegetarian/vegan options, like Basic Kitchen or Gnome Cafe.

faq.question: Which city is better for families with young children?
faq.answer: Savannah might have a slight edge for families with very young children due to its more relaxed pace and ample green spaces in the squares. Tybee Island is also a very accessible and family-friendly beach. Charleston, while wonderful, can feel a bit more geared towards adults with its fine dining and more formal attractions, though the Aquarium and nearby beaches are great for kids.

faq.question: What's the best time of year to visit either city?
faq.answer: Spring (March-May) and Fall (September-November) are ideal for both. The weather is pleasant (temperatures in the 60s-70s°F / 15-25°C), and humidity is lower. Summers (June-August) are very hot and humid, while winters (December-February) are mild but can still be chilly, with some attractions having reduced hours.

faq.question: Are Savannah and Charleston safe for solo travelers?
faq.answer: Both cities are generally safe for solo travelers, especially within their historic downtown areas where most attractions are located. Standard precautions apply, like being aware of your surroundings at night and avoiding poorly lit areas. Savannah's walkable layout and active nightlife make it feel very accessible for solo exploration.

faq.question: Which city has better guided tours?
faq.answer: Both cities excel in guided tours, offering a rich variety. Savannah is famous for its ghost tours (walking or trolley), which are incredibly popular and entertaining. Charleston offers excellent historical walking tours, carriage tours, and plantation tours that delve deep into its antebellum past. It really depends on your interest: spooky history vs. architectural and social history.

faq.question: What's the public transport like in Savannah vs Charleston?
faq.answer: Both historic districts are highly walkable, making extensive public transport less necessary for tourists. Charleston has the free DASH trolley system that loops through its historic area, which is very convenient. Savannah has a limited bus system, but most visitors rely on walking, ride-sharing, or trolley tours for getting around the core attractions.
